scope: Proposition 5.3 (Coupling the tilted paths) of the manuscript “A quadratic bound for Jacobsthal's function” (preprints/A-quadratic-bound-for-Jacobsthals-function-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 021 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f80267eebc82a9b8), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 25. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Choose sufficiently small absolute positive constants in the following order. For a permitted prime child of a state of type i, ratio s, and gap r, put t = r/x(p) − 1 and give that child mass q(p | r, s, i) = 1 p  t + 1 t 2 ϕi′ (t) ϕi(s) . (5.3) Only children with x(p) > ℓ and t ≤ S are retained. For ϵw = exp(−c2 √ log w) their total mass is at most 1 + ϵw. Dividing by 1 + ϵw and assigning the remaining mass to a cemetery state defines a killed Markov chain. This chain can be coupled with the continuous chain (4.16), killed at the first draw with x ≤ ℓ or t > S, so that the probability of failure is at most exp(−c3 √ log w). On success the chains have the same number of arrived-at states and matching exits. At corresponding states, |s − e s| ≤ h, log r e r ≤ CNh, h = 1 ⌈exp(c4 √ log w)⌉ . (5.4) All statements are uniform in sst ∈ [1.99, 2.3] and in the endpoint conventions stated above. For a length-m retained prefix, if Pw(p) denotes its probability in the killed chain, then the exact weight identity is h(p) = Pw(p)(1 + ϵw)m  r(p) rst 2 ϕe(sst) ϕi(s(p)) , (1 + ϵw)m = 1 + o(1).
